I invested 30 hours in this game and enjoyed it at the beginning until the tasks became too monotonous and repetitive.  I hired staff, four of them and they loafed around and followed the preprogrammed tasks as per the coding of the game.  Problems were they wouldn't empty trash cans when assigned cleaning.  They didn't restock shelves when supplies were in warehouse.  When they did restock, it was one box at a time and they had to travel between the warehouse and shop for each box (didn't use carts or take more than one box at a time).  In all, it was a learning experience to me to never buy a game like this as you take the risk of sorry programming (which this has some good points but also some bad) as I could have really kept going here.  I would have retained the game if I could have put employees in motion with tasks and they did them well.  When they loafed, i fired them....however, you have to run all over the place to see if they're loafing. I also want to make it clear that I love complicated strategy games. I play stellaris, dwarf fortress. I don't take issue with extreme depth and difficulty, but this is something else.

Game is..........ok at best, still missing tons of stuff.

Overall the idea behind the Serum system is ok and keeps you going back to base to stock and create serum, but the base upgrades are limited and VERY uninteresting, with little to no visual changes to the areas being "upgraded". While there are a few different types of serum you can make some are just....meh (damage resistance against a certain type, yay). No way to increase your stats so its an inventory management chore constantly with no improvement in sight (seriously, no serum to increase carrying capacity at least?).

Combat is very bland with the blocking, heavy attack and regular attack mechanic, not to mention no area effects such as explosives or triggerable elements on the map. Sometimes you get hit and dont even realize it due to the bad sound design and combat animations. its a "ugh" and you take damage, then dead. Tedious. Story. It's there, kind of. Lots of files to read and some information spread around but still not nearly enough to make it particularly interesting. Nothing anyone with any knowledge of typical sci-fi hasn't seen before, so don't expect any great twists.

A mediocre experience and one that I don't see getting a whole lot better unless they have an entire game behind this "demo" that wasn't revealed to us.

A mish-mash of solid concepts do not form together to make a good game.

While the artstyle and general 'vibe' of it seemed pretty great to me, and I was a vibe fan of the concept, the game just doesn't fit together that well.

The voice acting is distractedly dreadful, and I'd genuinely prefer none at all, since this isn't exactly a game that needs it, basically all the dialogue is poorly written and confusing, which works with a poor UI to make the game feel unnecessarily clunky.

The gameplay, honestly, is one of its worst sins. Don't even bother playing it with a controller. But if you use a mouse, you'll find the main thing that attracted me; It's clearly SUPPOSED to feel somewhat like Warthunder, but with an oddly weighty and slow style of handling, it feels outright awful to try and manuever your plane, with the game encouraging you to always go just a little slower than you'd be comfortable with. There's practically no sense of inertia, and gathering resources is tedious, and feels more or less like something that was slapped on to justify the game's resource system.

Also, there's the elephant in the room of the game's AI voice acting. I only found out about it shortly before I wrote this- It's choppy and sounds particularly weird, but at the same time, it feels like other parts of the game- The dialogue in particular, also used ML with how damned clunky it seems to be. I feel it must be restarted that this just... Adds up to something far, far worse than the sum of its parts. 

It's a shame too, since on the surface this game is made up of pretty much everything I SHOULD enjoy, but it just falls at the first hurdle.

The controls for this game are a little wonky. Using left click for most, if not all, of the controls is difficult, since plenty of other games uses "E" as the interact key. Then the movement is so fast; walking and sprinting in this game isn't that different. Also taking items out one by one after buying them is annoying. I didn't feel like finishing the tutorial since the controls were throwing me off.

Edit: I forgot to mention not being able to speed up the dialogue text. I have to wait for the whole thing to load...some of us read a little faster than that. Just having the option there would be cool.

What a shame. The first Chernobylite was a great game. The atmosphere and dark and gritty gameplay made for a nice mix of survival FPS and horror, with a base building element. I have absolutely no idea what would compel the developers to stray so far away from what made the first Chernobylite so great, but here we are. I even replayed the first game in preparation for this one when I saw it was releasing in a couple months only to be extremely disappointed.

The devs changed basically everything about the game for this, and from the very start of the game where you get to test the 3 'classes' it feels like an awfully made futuristic ubisoft shovelware clone. It's truly unbelievable as I loved the first game and was really looking forward to this one, but from what I can see, this game takes almost nothing from the first game, which wouldn't be an issue if the game was halfway decent.
	
There are now 6 classes, which specialize in melee, firearms, and chernobylite(magic), or a mix of the 3. They also changed the combat system to one that IMO resembles a mix of skyrim and a wannabe dark souls. Basically braindead AI that spam attacks you and you can block or dodge. Obviously the hitboxes are pretty bad and the game is sadly easy even on hard difficulty because you can just spam dodge and during the dodge animation you're unable to get hit, even if the shot goes straight through you. The NPCs and ESPECIALLY the player model look absolutely horrendus, they literally look and move like aliens who are pretending to be humans. It also seems like they picked and chose what lines would be voice acted by your character and others. I was 5 hours into the game and my character started talking in an unmistakably AI generated voice, and then 5 minutes later his normal voice comes back. Oh, and the game runs like absolute garbage even at the lowest settings and looks like garbage even at 'cinematic' settings.

If you enjoyed the first game and are looking for more of that, or even if you haven't played the first game, please just look at some gameplay videos, specifically of the combat, and you will see the vision that they have for this. It's a joke what they turned this game into. If you are looking for more of the first game, unfortunately this ain't it. 

To be completely honest even if the game looked good and ran well, I would still be extremely disappointed because this is such a jarring change from the first game that I'm surprised that they wouldn't just make a new title to ruin. RIP Chernobylite.

This is an amazing game with a few small and one big issue. The art style is amazing, unique and vibrant. Whilst I do have that issue with the AI voices, it is an exceptionally good game in all other areas, and I would recommend picking it up if you're looking for a more unique flying game.

[h2]It's a nice time waster, but not a deep game.[/h2]

[b]GRAPHICS[/b]
I like the low poly style, but the character models are really ugly. The tavern and the environment do look nice, though.

[b]SOUND[/b]
Nothing to write home about. Some AI was used, but I play these games while listening to podcasts / music, so I turn down the in-game sound anyway. 

[b]CONTROLS[/b]
WASD movement, jump button. You click on stuff to get work done. Some jobs are mini-games / QTEs, but they're laughably easy. Wood cutting is a bit janky. The toilet cleaning mini-game is bad, because it's just an unnecessary element of additional tedium (see below). Generally, I don't like QTEs / click timers, because they offer no real mechanical challenge, they just feel stupid. Especially the cooking could be much more interesting. Let players combine ingredients to create special variants of foods. 

[b]GAMEPLAY[/b]
It's NOT a management game. There's ZERO economical management. You never really run out of money. As the tavern grows, you get more money, so restocking the shelves always stays on the same difficulty level. Gameplay mostly revolves about completing mundane tasks (preparing food / drinks, fetching wood / water, cleaning). It's a time management game, first and foremost. The core loop is fine, you never run out of stuff to do. But you do have to accept that it's a very simple game. 

[b]PROBLEMS[/b]
The fairy helpers are kinda useless, because the cook / bartender ones always create "normal" quality items. They should be making better items as they level up. The waitress fairy gets stuck at times. The dishwashing one works fine.

The main issue of this game really is the tedium. Many gameplay elements solely exist to annoy you. Cleaning is the most obvious one. The game turns into "footprint remover simulator" in the later stages, as the fairies do most of the other jobs - unless you insist on creating perfect food / drink items. 

There are some "special" encounters (beggar, traveller) and some funny interactions (people passing out, thievery), but these are only interesting for like 2-3 times. Then they start to be annoying. The map contains some secrets, but it feels like there could be so much more. Maybe they'll add additional elements with future updates.

There's also some padding, especially level 8 is insane. You'll end up with more than 4x the money you actually need to level up and buy all the upgrades. This needs to be rebalanced. I really don't get why you have to meet arbitrary requirements like "sell 30 soups & 30 steaks". It feels unnatural and forced. In my opinion, this "quest" system doesn't offer any real challenge. It would be much better if there was more emergent gameplay. Challenges should be created by interacting systems (cleanliness of the tavern, service / food quality, and so on). There's already a reputation meter (which basically is an XP system), so unlocking the next tavern level doesn't need an additional layer of requirements. 

The prices of food / drink items are predetermined, you have no influence on them. It would be nice to have at least some kind of control over them. Low prices could attract more peasants with more lenient quality requirements, high prices mean that you have to be a great bartender / cook to keep the rich people coming.

Decoration is utterly meaningless right now, it doesn't really affect client quality. Tavern Master does this MUCH better.

Oh, and please add a way to auto-supply water to the washing / cooking stations in the late game. Running to the well is just... well, you know... tedious.

[b]SUMMARY[/b]
It's good for what it is, but it could be SO much better. It's a shallow game, so I can't quite recommend it. I've had some fun, but there's zero replayability.
